# Curated gene sets

**Curated layer markers, and the supplementary feature-plot panels.**

The first figure is a tile plot of canonical cortical layer markers: x-axis gene, y-axis cluster, colour is log2 fold-change. It answers a narrower question than the genome-wide heatmaps — how do the genes that *define* layer identity behave in each cluster?

The FigS11 and FigS12 panels that follow are UMAP feature plots split by genotype. Each gene occupies a row with wild-type and mutant side by side, and colour is expression with the scale shared within a gene so the two genotypes are directly comparable. They are drawn in batches of three genes: the full composite is written to file for use as a figure, but at ~2 columns by 12 rows it is unreadable when scaled into a report.

```{r customgeneset, fig.width=7, fig.height=9}
# Layer-marker tileplot. Fold changes are PSEUDOBULK from DE_combined_all:
# shared clusters = DKO-vs-WT, Misspecified = one-vs-rest.
custom_gene_set <- c("Eomes","Tbr1","Sox5","Fezf2","Tle4","Foxp2","Bcl11b",
                     "Satb2","Rorb","Etv1","Cux1","Pou3f1","Pou3f2","Lhx2","Cux2")
gene_set_label <- "Layer Markers"

logfc_table <- DE_combined_all %>%
  dplyr::filter(gene %in% custom_gene_set, cluster_named %in% PYR_SCOPE) %>%
  dplyr::select(gene, avg_log2FC, cluster = cluster_named)

if (!nrow(logfc_table)) {
  message("No matching genes for: ", gene_set_label)
} else {
  gene_order <- logfc_table %>% dplyr::group_by(gene) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(score = mean(abs(avg_log2FC), na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
    dplyr::arrange(desc(score)) %>% dplyr::pull(gene)
  plot_df <- logfc_table %>% dplyr::mutate(gene = factor(gene, levels = gene_order))

  n_genes    <- length(unique(plot_df$gene))
  n_clusters <- length(unique(plot_df$cluster))
  if (n_genes >= 2 && n_clusters >= 2) {
    p <- ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = gene, y = cluster, fill = avg_log2FC)) +
      geom_tile(color = "white") +
      scale_fill_gradient2(low = "blue", mid = "white", high = "red", midpoint = 0) +
      theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
      labs(title = paste("log2FC:", gene_set_label), x = "Gene", y = "Cluster",
           fill = "log2FC\n(shared=DKO/WT;\nMisspec=vs rest)") +
      theme(axis.text.x = element_text(size = 14, angle = 45, hjust = 1),
            axis.text.y = element_text(size = 14),
            plot.title  = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold")) +
      coord_fixed(ratio = 1)
    save_plot(p, file.path("custom_genes",
                           paste0(safe_name(gene_set_label), "_tileplot.pdf")),
              width = n_genes * 0.3 + 4, height = n_clusters * 0.3 + 2)
  }
}

# ---- FigS11 / FigS12 multi-gene FeaturePlots ----
FigS11_genes <- c("Grin1","Rbfox3","Satb2","Bcl11b","Cux1","Sox5",
                  "Tubb3","Dcx","Pou3f2","Fezf2","Rorb","Foxp2")
FigS12_genes <- c("Pcna","Sox2","Notch1","Dll1","Mki67","Top2a","Notch2","Hes5")

DefaultAssay(sc_seurat) <- "RNA"

# These are multi-gene FeaturePlots split by genotype, so the composite is very
# tall (2 columns x one row per gene). At full size it is unreadable when scaled
# into a report, so the composite is written to file for use as a figure and the
# report instead shows batches of a few genes at a time.
plot_feature_batches <- function(genes, tag, batch = 3) {
  genes <- intersect(genes, rownames(sc_seurat))
  if (!length(genes)) return(invisible(NULL))

  p_full <- FeaturePlot(sc_seurat, features = genes, coord.fixed = TRUE,
                        split.by = "Genotype", pt.size = 0.1, order = TRUE,
                        cols = c("lightblue", "darkblue"), keep.scale = "feature")
  save_plot(p_full, file.path("custom_genes", paste0(tag, "_gene_expression_all.pdf")),
            width = 12, height = 4 * length(genes), show = FALSE)

  idx <- split(seq_along(genes), ceiling(seq_along(genes) / batch))
  for (i in seq_along(idx)) {
    g <- genes[idx[[i]]]
    p <- FeaturePlot(sc_seurat, features = g, coord.fixed = TRUE,
                     split.by = "Genotype", pt.size = 0.1, order = TRUE,
                     cols = c("lightblue", "darkblue"), keep.scale = "feature")
    save_plot(p, file.path("custom_genes",
                           sprintf("%s_part%02d.pdf", tag, i)),
              width = 6, height = 3 * length(g))
  }
}

plot_feature_batches(FigS11_genes, "FigS11")
plot_feature_batches(FigS12_genes, "FigS12")
```

# Over-representation analysis (enrichGO)

**How the layer markers themselves redistribute.** The cluster-based analyses answer "how do the *groups* change"; these four figures ask "how do the *markers* change", which does not depend on where cluster boundaries were drawn. All are restricted to the pyramidal lineage and computed within genotype.

**1. Dumbbell plot.** For each layer marker, the percentage of nuclei in which it is detected: a grey point for wild-type, a red point for mutant, joined by a line whose length is the change. Markers are grouped by the panel they belong to. Read the *direction and length* of the lines — a clean upper-versus-deep swap would show all upper markers moving right and all deep markers moving left.

**2. Marker-score identity.** Each nucleus is scored against three marker panels and assigned to whichever scores highest, then composition is plotted per genotype. No cluster labels are used anywhere in this figure, so it is an independent check on the cluster-based composition.

**3. Upper versus deep score.** A two-dimensional density with the upper-layer score on x and the deep-layer score on y, one panel per genotype, with a diagonal marking equal scores. Nuclei with a clear identity sit off the diagonal; nuclei near it express both programmes or neither.

**4. Specification axis.** The same information collapsed to one number per nucleus — upper score minus deep score — plotted as a density per genotype. Zero means the two programmes are balanced; negative is deep-leaning, positive upper-leaning. A shift of the whole distribution is a shift in the balance of layer identity across the population.

```{r layer_marker_proportions, fig.width=9, fig.height=7, message=TRUE}
# =============================================================================
# PROPORTIONAL CHANGE OF LAYER MARKERS
#
# Four views, all restricted to the excitatory (projection-neuron) lineage and
# all computed within genotype so the ~2x recovery difference cancels:
#
#   1. dumbbell   - % of nuclei expressing each layer marker, WT vs DKO
#   2. identity   - each nucleus assigned to the marker panel it scores highest
#                   on, giving a composition that does not use cluster labels
#   3. 2D density - upper- vs deep-layer score per nucleus
#   4. axis       - distribution of (upper - deep) score, i.e. where each
#                   nucleus sits on the specification axis
# =============================================================================
LAYER_PANELS <- list(
  `Upper layer (L2/3-4)` = c("Cux1","Cux2","Satb2","Pou3f2","Pou3f3","Unc5d","Rorb"),
  `Deep layer (L5-6)`    = c("Bcl11b","Fezf2","Sox5","Tbr1","Foxp2","Tle4","Etv1","Nr4a2"),
  `Subplate / L6b`       = c("Nxph4","Cplx3","Ccn2","Ctgf","Lpar1","Moxd1"))
LAYER_PANELS <- lapply(LAYER_PANELS, intersect, y = rownames(sc_seurat))
PANEL_COLS <- c("Upper layer (L2/3-4)" = "#4C72B0",
                "Deep layer (L5-6)"    = "#DD8452",
                "Subplate / L6b"       = "#55A868")

neu <- cells_in_clusters(sc_seurat, PYR_SCOPE)
message("Marker analysis on ", ncol(neu), " excitatory-lineage nuclei; panels: ",
        paste(lengths(LAYER_PANELS), collapse = "/"), " genes")

# ---- 1. proportion of nuclei expressing each marker -------------------------
mk  <- unique(unlist(LAYER_PANELS))
key <- utils::stack(LAYER_PANELS); names(key) <- c("gene", "panel")
pct <- FetchData(neu, vars = c(mk, "Genotype")) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(all_of(mk), names_to = "gene", values_to = "e") %>%
  group_by(gene, Genotype) %>%
  summarise(pct = 100 * mean(e > 0), .groups = "drop") %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = Genotype, values_from = pct) %>%
  left_join(key, by = "gene") %>%
  mutate(delta = .data[[DKO]] - .data[[WT_LAB]],
         gene  = factor(gene, levels = gene[order(panel, delta)]))
save_table(pct %>% arrange(panel, desc(abs(delta))),
           "layer_marker_percent_expressing.csv")

p <- ggplot(pct) +
  geom_segment(aes(y = gene, yend = gene, x = .data[[WT_LAB]], xend = .data[[DKO]]),
               colour = "grey70", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(aes(y = gene, x = .data[[WT_LAB]], colour = "WT"), size = 3) +
  geom_point(aes(y = gene, x = .data[[DKO]], colour = "NeuroD2_D6DKO"), size = 3) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = GENOTYPE_COLORS, name = NULL) +
  facet_grid(panel ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "% of excitatory-lineage nuclei expressing marker", y = NULL,
       title = "Proportional change in layer-marker expression",
       subtitle = "within-genotype percentages, so uneven recovery cancels") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) + theme(strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 0))
save_plot(p, "layer_markers/marker_percent_expressing_dumbbell.pdf", 8, 7)

# ---- 2. identity from marker scores, not from clusters ----------------------
neu <- AddModuleScore(neu, features = LAYER_PANELS, name = "lp_", seed = 42)
sc_cols <- paste0("lp_", seq_along(LAYER_PANELS))
colnames(neu@meta.data)[match(sc_cols, colnames(neu@meta.data))] <- names(LAYER_PANELS)
md <- neu@meta.data[, c(names(LAYER_PANELS), "Genotype", "cluster_named")]
md$assigned <- names(LAYER_PANELS)[
  max.col(as.matrix(md[, names(LAYER_PANELS)]), ties.method = "first")]

comp_mk <- md %>% count(Genotype, assigned) %>% group_by(Genotype) %>%
  mutate(pct = 100 * n / sum(n)) %>% ungroup()
print(as.data.frame(comp_mk))
save_table(comp_mk, "layer_marker_identity_composition.csv")

p <- ggplot(comp_mk, aes(x = Genotype, y = pct, fill = assigned)) +
  geom_col(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = PANEL_COLS, name = "Best-scoring panel") +
  labs(y = "% of excitatory-lineage nuclei", x = NULL,
       title = "Identity assigned by layer-marker score",
       subtitle = "cluster labels not used") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11)
save_plot(p, "layer_markers/marker_score_identity_composition.pdf", 6, 5)

# ---- 3. upper vs deep score per nucleus -------------------------------------
p <- ggplot(md, aes(x = .data[[names(LAYER_PANELS)[1]]],
                    y = .data[[names(LAYER_PANELS)[2]]])) +
  geom_bin2d(bins = 60) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(trans = "log10", name = "nuclei") +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40") +
  facet_wrap(~Genotype) + coord_fixed() +
  labs(title = "Upper- versus deep-layer marker score, per nucleus",
       x = "Upper-layer score", y = "Deep-layer score") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11)
save_plot(p, "layer_markers/UL_vs_DL_score_density.pdf", 9, 5)

# ---- 4. the specification axis ----------------------------------------------
md$axis <- md[[names(LAYER_PANELS)[1]]] - md[[names(LAYER_PANELS)[2]]]
p <- ggplot(md, aes(x = axis, fill = Genotype, colour = Genotype)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.35, linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = GENOTYPE_COLORS) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = GENOTYPE_COLORS) +
  labs(x = "upper-layer score  -  deep-layer score", y = "density",
       title = "Position of each nucleus on the upper/deep specification axis",
       subtitle = "left = deep-layer character, right = upper-layer character") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11)
save_plot(p, "layer_markers/specification_axis_density.pdf", 8, 5)

axis_summary <- md %>% group_by(Genotype) %>%
  summarise(median_axis = round(median(axis), 3),
            pct_upper_leaning = round(100 * mean(axis > 0), 1), .groups = "drop")
print(as.data.frame(axis_summary))
save_table(axis_summary, "layer_marker_specification_axis.csv")
rm(neu); invisible(gc(verbose = FALSE))
```

**Requested interneuron and vascular markers.** UMAP feature plots (pooled and split by genotype) and per-cluster violins for a specific marker panel.

The detection-rate table printed above the plots should be read first. At E15 most mature interneuron subclass markers are barely expressed — several are detected in well under 1% of nuclei — so the corresponding feature plots are close to empty. That absence is itself the result: these subclass identities have not yet been established at this age. Any marker not present in the expression matrix at all is listed explicitly rather than silently skipped.

```{r requested_marker_panel, fig.width=9, fig.height=5}
REQUESTED_MARKERS <- c("Lamp5", "Meis2", "Pvalb", "Sst", "Vip", "Sncg")
VLMC_MARKERS      <- c("Slc6a13", "Dcn", "Col1a1", "Lum", "Ptgds")
PANEL_GENES <- c(REQUESTED_MARKERS, VLMC_MARKERS)

available <- intersect(PANEL_GENES, rownames(sc_seurat))
absent    <- setdiff(PANEL_GENES, rownames(sc_seurat))
if (length(absent))
  cat("Not in the expression matrix (fewer than 3 nuclei at object creation): ",
      paste(absent, collapse = ", "), "\n", sep = "")

detect <- FetchData(sc_seurat, vars = c(available, "Genotype")) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(all_of(available), names_to = "gene", values_to = "e") %>%
  group_by(gene, Genotype) %>%
  summarise(pct_expressing = round(100 * mean(e > 0), 3),
            mean_expr = round(mean(e), 4), .groups = "drop") %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = Genotype,
                     values_from = c(pct_expressing, mean_expr))
print(as.data.frame(detect))
save_table(detect, "requested_marker_detection_rates.csv")

save_feature_plots(sc_seurat, genes = available, reduction = "umap",
                   plotdir = "requested_markers")
save_feature_plots_split(sc_seurat, genes = available, reduction = "umap",
                         plotdir = "requested_markers")

plan_fork()
invisible(future.apply::future_lapply(available, function(gene) {
  worker_setup()
  p <- suppressMessages(VlnPlot(sc_seurat, features = gene, group.by = "cluster_named",
               split.by = "Genotype", cols = GENOTYPE_COLORS, pt.size = 0.1)) +
    ggtitle(gene) +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
          axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
  save_plot(p, file.path("requested_markers",
                         paste0(gene, "_violin_by_cluster.pdf")),
            9, 4, quiet = TRUE, show = FALSE)
}, future.seed = TRUE))
cat("Requested-marker panel written for", length(available), "genes:",
    paste(available, collapse = ", "), "\n")
```

**Over-representation analysis.** Unlike GSEA, which uses the whole ranked list, this asks whether a fixed set of strongly changed genes contains more members of a GO term than chance would predict.

The **dot plot** is faceted by direction — genes up in the mutant on one side, down on the other. X-axis is cluster, y-axis term, colour is −log10(adjusted p), and point size is the number of genes from the query set found in that term. The **per-term tile plots** that follow have the same construction as the GSEA ones: genes on x, clusters on y, colour is pseudobulk log2 fold-change.

```{r enrichGO, fig.width=14, fig.height=9}
# =============================================================================
# ORA with gene sets defined by PSEUDOBULK EFFECT SIZE, not per-cell FindMarkers
# p-values (invalid at n = 1). Genes are selected by |pseudobulk log2FC| from
# DE_combined_all and split up/down by sign. Shared clusters = DKO-vs-WT;
# Misspecified = one-vs-rest. No per-gene significance is claimed.
# =============================================================================
LOG2FC_CUTOFF <- 1
MIN_CPM_ORA   <- 5

# Minimum genes a GO term must contain to be eligible for the summary dotplot.
# The 2026 file used 10. A ~150-gene ORA query overlaps a GO:BP term in a
# handful of genes, so at 10 only 4 of 14 clusters contributed any term and the
# dotplot was effectively the Misspecified cluster alone; at 5 it is 12 of 14.
ORA_MIN_COUNT <- 5

ORA_CLUSTERS <- intersect(NEURONAL_CLUSTERS,
                          as.character(unique(DE_combined_all$cluster_named)))

#' enrichGO on one gene vector, returning the result table with a rich factor.
#' OrgDb is passed as a string so this is safe in a fresh worker session. Note
#' this function runs inside multisession workers, which do not inherit attached
#' packages - so everything here is either base R or :: qualified (no %>%).
run_enrichGO <- function(genes) {
  if (length(genes) < 5) return(NULL)
  go <- clusterProfiler::enrichGO(
    gene = genes, OrgDb = "org.Mm.eg.db", keyType = "SYMBOL", ont = "BP",
    readable = FALSE, minGSSize = 10, maxGSSize = 300,
    pAdjustMethod = "BH", pvalueCutoff = 0.05, qvalueCutoff = 0.2)
  if (is.null(go) || !nrow(go@result)) return(NULL)
  res <- as.data.frame(go@result)
  ratio_num <- function(x) vapply(strsplit(x, "/"),
                                  function(p) as.numeric(p[1]) / as.numeric(p[2]),
                                  numeric(1))
  res$GeneRatio_num <- ratio_num(res$GeneRatio)
  res$BgRatio_num   <- ratio_num(res$BgRatio)
  res$RichFactor    <- res$GeneRatio_num / res$BgRatio_num
  res
}

# Gene vectors are built up front (cheap, and keeps the DE tables out of the
# workers), then the ORA calls themselves run in parallel.
ora_gene_sets <- c(
  lapply(setNames(ORA_CLUSTERS, ORA_CLUSTERS), function(clust) {
    de_c <- DE_combined_all %>%
      dplyr::filter(cluster_named == clust, !is.na(avg_log2FC),
                    mean_cpm > MIN_CPM_ORA)
    list(up   = de_c %>% dplyr::filter(avg_log2FC >  LOG2FC_CUTOFF) %>% dplyr::pull(gene),
         down = de_c %>% dplyr::filter(avg_log2FC < -LOG2FC_CUTOFF) %>% dplyr::pull(gene))
  }),
  list(all = local({
    de_c <- DE %>% dplyr::filter(!is.na(avg_log2FC), mean_cpm > MIN_CPM_ORA)
    list(up   = de_c %>% dplyr::filter(avg_log2FC >  LOG2FC_CUTOFF) %>% dplyr::pull(gene),
         down = de_c %>% dplyr::filter(avg_log2FC < -LOG2FC_CUTOFF) %>% dplyr::pull(gene))
  }))
)
for (nm in names(ora_gene_sets)) {
  message("enrichGO input '", nm, "': ", length(ora_gene_sets[[nm]]$up), " up / ",
          length(ora_gene_sets[[nm]]$down), " down genes")
}

plan_session()
go_enrich_raw <- future.apply::future_lapply(ora_gene_sets, function(gs) {
  worker_setup()
  res <- list()
  go_up   <- run_enrichGO(gs$up)
  go_down <- run_enrichGO(gs$down)
  if (!is.null(go_up))   { go_up$direction   <- "up";   res$up   <- go_up   }
  if (!is.null(go_down)) { go_down$direction <- "down"; res$down <- go_down }
  if (!length(res)) return(NULL)
  dplyr::bind_rows(res)
}, future.seed = TRUE)
names(go_enrich_raw) <- names(ora_gene_sets)
go_enrich_results <- purrr::compact(go_enrich_raw)

for (nm in names(go_enrich_results)) {
  save_table(go_enrich_results[[nm]] %>% dplyr::select(dplyr::any_of(
               c("ID","Description","direction","GeneRatio","BgRatio","RichFactor",
                 "pvalue","p.adjust","qvalue","Count","geneID"))),
             file.path("enrichGO", paste0("enrichGO_", safe_name(nm), ".csv")))
}

if (!length(go_enrich_results)) {
  message("No enrichGO results - try lowering LOG2FC_CUTOFF")
} else {
  top_terms <- go_enrich_results %>%
    purrr::imap_dfr(~ .x %>% dplyr::filter(p.adjust < 0.05, Count >= ORA_MIN_COUNT) %>%
                      dplyr::arrange(desc(RichFactor)) %>% dplyr::slice_head(n = 3) %>%
                      dplyr::mutate(cluster = .y))

  plot_data <- purrr::imap_dfr(go_enrich_results, function(res, cl) {
    res %>% dplyr::filter(Description %in% top_terms$Description) %>%
      dplyr::mutate(cluster = cl)
  })

  if (nrow(plot_data)) {
    df_ora <- plot_data %>%
      dplyr::select(Description, cluster, direction, GeneRatio_num,
                    p.adjust, Count, RichFactor) %>%
      dplyr::mutate(logFDR = -log10(p.adjust),
                    direction = factor(direction, levels = c("up", "down")),
                    Description = factor(Description, levels = rev(unique(Description))))

    p <- ggplot(df_ora, aes(x = cluster, y = Description)) +
      geom_point(aes(color = logFDR, size = Count)) +
      scale_color_gradient(low = "blue", high = "red") +
      scale_size_area(max_size = 10) +
      theme_minimal() +
      labs(x = "Cluster", y = "GO:BP term", size = "Gene count",
           color = "-log10(adj. p)",
           title = paste0("ORA (enrichGO) - neuronal | |log2FC|>", LOG2FC_CUTOFF,
                          " [Misspecified = vs rest]")) +
      theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) +
      facet_wrap(~direction)
    save_plot(p, "enrichGO/enrichGO_dot_plot_combined.pdf", 12, 8)
  }

  # ---- Gene-by-cluster tileplots for the ORA terms ----
  ora_top_terms <- go_enrich_results %>%
    purrr::imap_dfr(~ .x %>% dplyr::filter(p.adjust < 0.05) %>%
                      dplyr::arrange(p.adjust) %>% dplyr::slice_head(n = 80) %>%
                      dplyr::select(Description)) %>%
    dplyr::distinct(Description) %>% dplyr::pull(Description)

  ora_term_to_clusters <- go_enrich_results %>%
    purrr::imap_dfr(function(res, cl) {
      res %>% dplyr::filter(Description %in% ora_top_terms) %>%
        dplyr::distinct(Description) %>% dplyr::mutate(cluster = cl)
    }) %>% dplyr::group_by(Description) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(clusters = paste(sort(unique(cluster)), collapse = ", "),
                     .groups = "drop")

  ora_term_genes <- collect_term_genes(go_enrich_results, ora_top_terms,
                                       gene_col = "geneID")

  if (!nrow(ora_term_genes)) {
    message("No enrichGO term genes for tileplots")
  } else {
    ora_term_logfc <- ora_term_genes %>%
      dplyr::left_join(logfc_for_genes(DE_combined_all, unique(ora_term_genes$gene),
                                       c(ORA_CLUSTERS, "all"), DE),
                       by = "gene", relationship = "many-to-many") %>%
      dplyr::filter(!is.na(avg_log2FC))
    render_term_tileplots(ora_term_logfc, ora_term_to_clusters,
                          "enrichGO/Genes_by_cluster")
  }
}
```

# Gene sets for the per-gene figures

Assembles the gene list used for the per-gene violin and UMAP figures: the strongly changed genes, a curated always-include list, and the top markers of the misspecified cluster. No figures.

```{r gene_sets}
# Defined in its own chunk because the violin chunk below is disabled by default
# but the UMAP export chunk still needs this list. (In the 2026 file this vector
# was created inside the violin chunk, so skipping violins broke the UMAPs.)

# Top one-vs-rest genes for the Misspecified cluster, so the strongest markers of
# the aberrant population are always plotted even if they miss the shared cutoffs.
N_MISSPEC_TOP <- 25

misspec_top_genes <- DE_combined_all %>%
  dplyr::filter(comparison == "Misspec_vs_Rest", !is.na(avg_log2FC), mean_cpm > 5) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(cluster_named) %>%
  dplyr::group_modify(~ dplyr::bind_rows(
    dplyr::slice_max(.x, avg_log2FC, n = N_MISSPEC_TOP),
    dplyr::slice_min(.x, avg_log2FC, n = N_MISSPEC_TOP))) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup() %>% dplyr::pull(gene) %>% unique()

# Curated genes that always get a plot regardless of selection.
PLOT_ALWAYS <- unique(c(
  "Nr4a2","Rorb","Neurod1","Satb2","Bcl11b","Fezf2","Unc5d","Cux2","Cux1","Eomes",
  "Pax6","Tbr1","Neurod2","Neurod6","Btg2","Id2","Id3","Epha3","Robo2","Top2a",
  "Hs6st3","Tafa2","Gad1","Gad2","Lhx6","Reln","Rmst","Nfib","Zbtb20","Cdk14",
  "Sox6","Npas3","Scrt2","Ntng2","Sox2ot","Dach1","Dpp10","Tcf7l2","Dgkg",
  "Gabra2","Elmod1","Fam135b","Hhip","Gpat3","Adcy7","Dkk2","Scube2","Crlf1",
  "Sox2","Mki67","Pcna","Tubb3","Dcx","Map2","Ncam1","Rbfox3","Gap43","Egfr",
  "Bdnf","Eno2","Pou3f3","Pou3f2","Sox5","Pou3f1","Olig2","Hes1","Hes5","Notch1",
  "Notch2","Robo1","Ebf1","Grin1","Ebf2","Ebf3","Dll1","Kdm1a","Hdac9","Cdkn1c",
  "Insm1","Smarcd3","Dpf3","Tiam2","Pak3","Hes6","Gadd45g","Prox1","Emx2","Nhlh1",
  "Ptprd","Bcl11a","Lmo1","Sema3a","Sema3c","Hrk","Runx1t1","Cxcr4","Ackr3",
  "Dlx2","Pvalb","Sst","Htr3a","Mast1","Adck1"))

PLOT_GENES <- Reduce(union, list(genes_pyr_fc, FORCE_GENES,
                                 PLOT_ALWAYS, misspec_top_genes))
PLOT_GENES <- intersect(PLOT_GENES, rownames(sc_seurat))

message("Per-gene figure set: ", length(PLOT_GENES), " genes across ",
        length(PYR_SCOPE), " pyramidal clusters")
save_table(data.frame(gene = PLOT_GENES), "per_gene_figure_gene_list.csv")
```

**Violin plots, five views per gene.** A violin shows the full distribution of expression rather than just a mean, which matters for single-cell data where a gene is often off in most nuclei and high in a few.

1. **Split across clusters** — one panel per gene, clusters on the x-axis, wild-type and mutant drawn side by side.
2. **Per cluster** — the same comparison one cluster at a time, so a single population can be inspected without the others compressing the axis.
3. **Per cluster, non-zero nuclei only** — identical to (2) but excluding nuclei where the gene is undetected. When a gene is expressed in a minority of cells the zeros dominate the shape and hide any difference in the cells that do express it.
4. **All clusters, non-zero, dodged.**
5. **Pooled across pyramidal clusters** — cluster identity collapsed, giving a single genotype comparison per gene.

Several thousand files are written to `plots/Violin/`; they are not embedded in this report.

```{r DE_gene_plots}
# =============================================================================
# VIOLIN PLOTS. Thousands of individual PDFs - the slowest chunk in the file.
#
# NOTE on the Misspecified cluster: it has no WT cells, so its within-cluster
# genotype violins (sections 2-3) are single-sided. The DKO distribution still
# renders; there is simply no WT to compare against inside that cluster, which
# mirrors the heatmap logic.
#
# Sections 4 and 5 in the 2026 file iterated over a leftover 9-gene scratch
# vector named `temp` instead of the real gene set - fixed here.
#
# PARALLELISATION SHAPE. Sections 2 and 3 produce one plot per gene x cluster
# (~250 x 10 = 2500 each). Subsetting the Seurat object inside that loop would
# mean ~5000 subsets of a 31k-cell object and would dominate the runtime, so the
# loop is inverted: fan out over CLUSTERS, subset once per cluster in the worker,
# then loop genes inside. 10 subsets instead of 5000.
# =============================================================================
viol_dir <- "Violin"
n_genes    <- length(PLOT_GENES)
n_clusters <- length(PYR_SCOPE)

# Pyramidal subset used by every section, built once with ordered cluster levels.
pyramids_seurat <- cells_in_clusters(sc_seurat, PYR_SCOPE)
pyramids_seurat$cluster_named <- factor(as.character(pyramids_seurat$cluster_named),
                                        levels = PYR_SCOPE)
DefaultAssay(pyramids_seurat) <- "RNA"

message("Violins: ", n_genes, " genes x ", n_clusters, " clusters -> ~",
        format(2 * n_genes * n_clusters + 3 * n_genes, big.mark = ","), " PDFs")

plan_fork()

# ---- 1. All clusters, split violin ----
message("=== Section 1: all-cluster split violins (", n_genes, " genes) ===")
invisible(future.apply::future_lapply(PLOT_GENES, function(gene) {
  worker_setup()
  p <- suppressMessages(VlnPlot(pyramids_seurat, features = gene, group.by = "cluster_named",
               split.by = "Genotype", cols = GENOTYPE_COLORS, pt.size = 0.1)) +
    ggtitle(gene) +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
          axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
  save_plot(p, file.path(viol_dir, "default",
                         paste0(gene, "_all_clusters_violin.pdf")), 8, 4, quiet = TRUE, show = FALSE)
}, future.seed = TRUE))

# ---- 2 + 3. Per cluster: default violin and non-zero-only violin ----
# One worker per cluster; each subsets once, then loops its genes and writes both
# the default and the non-zero plot for each.
message("=== Sections 2+3: per-cluster violins (", n_genes * n_clusters,
        " gene x cluster pairs, fanned out over ", n_clusters, " clusters) ===")
invisible(future.apply::future_lapply(PYR_SCOPE, function(cluster) {
  worker_setup()
  sub  <- cells_in_clusters(pyramids_seurat, cluster)
  safe <- safe_name(cluster)
  # Fetch every gene for this cluster once, rather than per plot.
  expr_all <- FetchData(sub, vars = c(intersect(PLOT_GENES, rownames(sub)), "Genotype"))
  for (gene in intersect(PLOT_GENES, rownames(sub))) {
    # 2. default violin, all cells
    p <- suppressMessages(VlnPlot(sub, features = gene, group.by = "Genotype",
                 cols = GENOTYPE_COLORS, pt.size = 0.1)) +
      ggtitle(paste0(gene, " - ", cluster)) +
      theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))
    save_plot(p, file.path(viol_dir, "default",
                           paste0(gene, "-", safe, "_violin.pdf")), 4, 4, quiet = TRUE, show = FALSE)

    # 3. non-zero cells only
    expr <- expr_all[expr_all[[gene]] > 0, c(gene, "Genotype"), drop = FALSE]
    if (!nrow(expr)) next
    p <- ggplot(expr, aes(x = Genotype, y = .data[[gene]], fill = Genotype)) +
      geom_violin(trim = FALSE, scale = "width") +
      geom_jitter(width = 0.2, size = 0.5, alpha = 0.5) +
      scale_fill_manual(values = GENOTYPE_COLORS) +
      theme_minimal() + ggtitle(paste0(gene, " - ", cluster)) + ylab("Expression") +
      theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))
    save_plot(p, file.path(viol_dir, "nonzero",
                           paste0(gene, "-", safe, "_nonzero_violin.pdf")), 4, 4, quiet = TRUE, show = FALSE)
  }
  message("  violins done for cluster: ", cluster)
  NULL
}, future.seed = TRUE))

# ---- 4. All clusters, non-zero, dodged ----
message("=== Section 4: all-cluster nonzero violins ===")
invisible(future.apply::future_lapply(PLOT_GENES, function(gene) {
  worker_setup()
  expr <- FetchData(pyramids_seurat, vars = c(gene, "cluster_named", "Genotype")) %>%
    dplyr::filter(.data[[gene]] > 0)
  if (!nrow(expr)) return(NULL)
  p <- ggplot(expr, aes(x = cluster_named, y = .data[[gene]], fill = Genotype)) +
    geom_violin(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), trim = FALSE, scale = "width") +
    geom_jitter(position = position_jitterdodge(jitter.width = 0.2, dodge.width = 0.8),
                size = 0.5, alpha = 0.5) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = GENOTYPE_COLORS) +
    theme_minimal() + ggtitle(gene) + ylab("Expression") +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
          axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
  save_plot(p, file.path(viol_dir, "nonzero",
                         paste0(gene, "_all_clusters_nonzero_violin.pdf")), 9, 4, quiet = TRUE, show = FALSE)
}, future.seed = TRUE))

# ---- 5. Pooled across all pyramidal clusters ----
message("=== Section 5: pooled pyramidal violins ===")
invisible(future.apply::future_lapply(PLOT_GENES, function(gene) {
  worker_setup()
  p <- suppressMessages(VlnPlot(pyramids_seurat, features = gene, group.by = "Genotype",
               cols = GENOTYPE_COLORS, pt.size = 0)) +
    ggtitle(paste0(gene, " - all pyramidal cells")) +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5)) + NoLegend()
  save_plot(p, file.path(viol_dir, "pooled",
                         paste0(gene, "_pooled_pyramids_violin.pdf")),
              width = 2.2, height = 5, quiet = TRUE, show = FALSE)
}, future.seed = TRUE))

cat("Violin plots complete:", length(PLOT_GENES), "genes x ",
    length(PYR_SCOPE), "clusters, written to plots/Violin/\n")
```

**Per-gene UMAP feature plots.** One figure per gene showing where in the embedding that gene is expressed, pooled and split by genotype, written to `plots/gene_umaps/`. Not embedded in this report — there are several hundred.

```{r DE_gene_umaps}
# FeaturePlot UMAPs for the same gene set, on the standard "umap" embedding.
# A slim copy keeps each worker's memory footprint small.
umap_obj <- DietSeurat(sc_seurat, features = PLOT_GENES, assays = "RNA",
                       dimreducs = c("umap", "ref.umap"))
message("Exporting UMAPs for ", length(PLOT_GENES), " genes")

save_feature_plots(umap_obj, genes = PLOT_GENES,
                   reduction = "umap", plotdir = "gene_umaps")
save_feature_plots_split(umap_obj, genes = PLOT_GENES,
                         reduction = "umap", plotdir = "gene_umaps")
rm(umap_obj); invisible(gc(verbose = FALSE))
```

# Cell-type proportions

**Cell-type composition by genotype.** Three figures.

The **stacked bar** gives the full composition of each genotype, every cluster as a band whose height is its share of that genotype's nuclei. Both bars sum to 100%, so this shows relative composition and not absolute cell numbers.

The **grouped bar** collapses the layer clusters into upper-layer, deep-layer and the DKO-specific population, which is the comparison of interest.

The **dot plot** shows, for every cluster, the log2 ratio of its mutant to wild-type proportion: right of the dashed line means enriched in the mutant, left means depleted, and point size reflects how common the cluster is. Its usefulness here is the spread — values on both sides of zero cannot be produced by a uniform difference in cell recovery.

All of this is descriptive: with one animal per genotype these proportions are single observations and no significance test is valid.

```{r proportion_analysis}
# =============================================================================
# Compositional shift, DKO vs WT. DESCRIPTIVE ONLY: with n = 1 per genotype the
# proportions are single observations, so no significance test is valid (a
# cell-level test would be pseudoreplicated). We report counts, within-genotype
# proportions and the DKO/WT ratio.
# =============================================================================
comp <- sc_seurat@meta.data %>%
  dplyr::count(cluster_named, Genotype, name = "n_cells") %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = Genotype, values_from = n_cells, values_fill = 0) %>%
  mutate(prop_WT    = .data[[WT_LAB]] / tot_WT,
         prop_DKO   = .data[[DKO]]    / tot_DKO,
         log2_ratio = log2((prop_DKO + 1e-4) / (prop_WT + 1e-4)),
         pct_WT     = round(100 * prop_WT, 2),
         pct_DKO    = round(100 * prop_DKO, 2)) %>%
  arrange(desc(log2_ratio))

save_table(comp, "celltype_proportions_DKO_vs_WT.csv")
print(comp %>% dplyr::select(cluster_named, !!WT_LAB, !!DKO,
                             pct_WT, pct_DKO, log2_ratio))

# ---- Upper-layer vs deep-layer summary ----
UL_CLUSTERS <- c("Layer II/III", "Layer IV")
DL_CLUSTERS <- c("Layer V", "Layer VI", "Layer VIb")
FATE_LEVELS <- c("Upper-layer (UL)", "Deep-layer (DL)", PRIVATE_CLUSTERS)

fate_summary <- sc_seurat@meta.data %>%
  mutate(fate = dplyr::case_when(
    cluster_named %in% UL_CLUSTERS      ~ "Upper-layer (UL)",
    cluster_named %in% DL_CLUSTERS      ~ "Deep-layer (DL)",
    cluster_named %in% PRIVATE_CLUSTERS ~ as.character(cluster_named),
    TRUE ~ "Other")) %>%
  dplyr::filter(fate != "Other") %>%
  dplyr::count(fate, Genotype, name = "n_cells") %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = Genotype, values_from = n_cells, values_fill = 0) %>%
  mutate(prop_WT    = .data[[WT_LAB]] / tot_WT,
         prop_DKO   = .data[[DKO]]    / tot_DKO,
         pct_WT     = round(100 * prop_WT, 2),
         pct_DKO    = round(100 * prop_DKO, 2),
         log2_ratio = round(log2((prop_DKO + 1e-4) / (prop_WT + 1e-4)), 3)) %>%
  arrange(desc(log2_ratio))

print(fate_summary)
save_table(fate_summary, "UL_DL_fate_proportions.csv")

# ---- 1. Stacked composition, every cluster ----
comp_long <- sc_seurat@meta.data %>%
  dplyr::count(cluster_named, Genotype, name = "n") %>%
  group_by(Genotype) %>% mutate(prop = n / sum(n)) %>% ungroup()

# The stacked bar carries ~20 categories, so the default hue wheel makes
# neighbouring segments hard to tell apart. Use a divergent HCL ramp across the
# ordered cluster levels and separate the segments with thin white borders.
# (The UMAPs and heatmap annotations keep the Seurat default palette.)
# "Spectral" is diverging and puts several near-white colours in the middle of
# a 20+ category ramp, which read as missing segments (Layer IV looked
# transparent). "Zissou 1" spans the same warm-to-cool range with a maximum
# luminance of 0.78, so every category stays visible.
STACK_PALETTE <- setNames(
  grDevices::hcl.colors(nlevels(comp_long$cluster_named), "Zissou 1"),
  levels(comp_long$cluster_named))

p_stack <- ggplot(comp_long, aes(x = Genotype, y = prop, fill = cluster_named)) +
  geom_col(position = "stack", colour = "white", linewidth = 0.15) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = STACK_PALETTE) +
  labs(y = "Proportion of cells", x = NULL, fill = "Cluster",
       title = "Cell-type composition by genotype (n=1 each; descriptive)") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.text = element_text(size = 7), legend.key.size = unit(3, "mm"))
save_plot(p_stack, "proportions/composition_stacked.pdf", 7, 8)

# ---- 2. UL / DL / Misspecified grouped bar ----
# Levels are taken from FATE_LEVELS, which is built from PRIVATE_CLUSTERS. In the
# 2026 file this list was hardcoded to "Misspecified" while case_when() emitted
# "Misspecified UL"/"DL", so those bars silently dropped out as NA.
fate_long <- fate_summary %>%
  dplyr::select(fate, pct_WT, pct_DKO) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(pct_WT, pct_DKO), names_to = "Genotype", values_to = "pct") %>%
  mutate(Genotype = ifelse(Genotype == "pct_WT", "WT", "DKO"),
         Genotype = factor(Genotype, levels = c("WT", "DKO")),
         fate     = factor(fate, levels = FATE_LEVELS))
stopifnot(!any(is.na(fate_long$fate)))

p_fate <- ggplot(fate_long, aes(x = fate, y = pct, fill = Genotype)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), width = 0.7) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("WT" = "grey70", "DKO" = "firebrick")) +
  labs(y = "% of genotype's cells", x = NULL,
       title = "UL vs DL neuronal proportions (n=1 each; descriptive)") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 20, hjust = 1))
save_plot(p_fate, "proportions/UL_DL_fate_barplot.pdf", 6, 5)

# ---- 3. log2-ratio dotplot: which clusters expand or contract in DKO ----
p_ratio <- comp %>%
  mutate(cluster_named = factor(cluster_named,
                                levels = cluster_named[order(log2_ratio)])) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = log2_ratio, y = cluster_named,
             color = log2_ratio > 0, size = pmax(pct_WT, pct_DKO))) +
  geom_point() + geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("FALSE" = "steelblue", "TRUE" = "firebrick"),
                     labels = c("Depleted in DKO", "Enriched in DKO"), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "log2(DKO prop / WT prop)", y = NULL, size = "max % cells",
       title = "Compositional shift by cluster (n=1 each; descriptive)") +
  theme_minimal()
save_plot(p_ratio, "proportions/compositional_shift_dotplot.pdf", 7, 7)

message("Proportion analysis complete. NOTE: single replicate per genotype - ",
        "proportions are descriptive, no significance test is valid.")
```

# Interneurons

**Interneuron changes.** The printed tables report whether *Neurod2* and *Neurod6* are expressed in the interneuron clusters at all, and how many genes change substantially in each.

The figure is an **MA-style plot**, one panel per interneuron cluster: x-axis is mean expression, y-axis is the log2 fold-change, dashed lines mark the two-fold threshold, and points beyond it are highlighted. It is deliberately not a volcano plot — there are no p-values to put on a y-axis here — so read it as effect size against expression level, where changes at low expression are the least trustworthy.

```{r interneuron_analysis}
in_present <- intersect(INTERNEURON_CLUSTERS, CLUSTERS_PRESENT)

# ---- Are Neurod2/Neurod6 actually expressed in interneurons here? ----
# Both are reported as only weakly expressed here; confirm in this data before
# interpreting any interneuron effect. Pyramidal clusters included as reference.
nd_genes <- intersect(c("Neurod2", "Neurod6"), rownames(sc_seurat))
nd_expr <- FetchData(sc_seurat, vars = c(nd_genes, "cluster_named", "Genotype")) %>%
  dplyr::filter(cluster_named %in% c(in_present, "Layer V", "Layer II/III")) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(all_of(nd_genes), names_to = "gene", values_to = "expr") %>%
  group_by(cluster_named, Genotype, gene) %>%
  summarise(mean_expr = mean(expr), pct_expr = 100 * mean(expr > 0), .groups = "drop")
save_table(nd_expr, "interneuron_NeuroD_expression.csv")
print(nd_expr)

# ---- Pseudobulk DKO-vs-WT per interneuron cluster ----
# These are shared clusters with both genotypes present, so the within-cluster
# contrast IS defined here, unlike the Misspecified cluster.
interneuron_DE <- DE_combined_all %>%
  dplyr::filter(cluster_named %in% in_present, comparison == "DKO_vs_WT")

if (!nrow(interneuron_DE)) {
  message("No interneuron clusters passed the pseudobulk cell-count threshold.")
} else {
  save_table(interneuron_DE, "interneuron_DKO_vs_WT_pseudobulk.csv")

  change_summary <- interneuron_DE %>%
    dplyr::filter(mean_cpm > 5) %>%
    group_by(cluster_named) %>%
    summarise(n_tested       = n(),
              n_up_fc1       = sum(avg_log2FC >  1, na.rm = TRUE),
              n_down_fc1     = sum(avg_log2FC < -1, na.rm = TRUE),
              max_abs_log2FC = round(max(abs(avg_log2FC), na.rm = TRUE), 2),
              .groups = "drop")
  print(change_summary)
  save_table(change_summary, "interneuron_change_summary.csv")

  top_changed <- interneuron_DE %>%
    dplyr::filter(mean_cpm > 5) %>%
    group_by(cluster_named) %>%
    slice_max(abs(avg_log2FC), n = 20) %>%
    arrange(cluster_named, desc(avg_log2FC)) %>%
    dplyr::select(cluster_named, gene, avg_log2FC, cpm_WT, cpm_DKO, mean_cpm)
  save_table(top_changed, "interneuron_top_changed_genes.csv")

  # MA-style plot per cluster (log2FC vs mean expression - there are no p-values)
  p_ma <- interneuron_DE %>%
    dplyr::filter(mean_cpm > 1) %>%
    mutate(changed = abs(avg_log2FC) > 1) %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = log2(mean_cpm + 1), y = avg_log2FC, color = changed)) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.4, size = 0.6) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = c(-1, 1), linetype = "dashed") +
    scale_color_manual(values = c("FALSE" = "grey70", "TRUE" = "firebrick"),
                       labels = c("|log2FC|<=1", "|log2FC|>1"), name = NULL) +
    facet_wrap(~cluster_named) +
    labs(x = "log2(mean CPM + 1)", y = "log2FC (DKO vs WT)",
         title = "Interneuron DKO-vs-WT changes (descriptive; n=1 per genotype)") +
    theme_minimal()
  save_plot(p_ma, "interneurons/interneuron_MA_plots.pdf", 10, 4)
}

# ---- Surface the interneuron GSEA results already computed above ----
for (cl in intersect(in_present, names(gsea_results))) {
  df <- get_gsea_df(gsea_results[[cl]]) %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(p.adjust)) %>% arrange(p.adjust) %>% head(20)
  if (nrow(df)) {
    save_table(df %>% dplyr::select(dplyr::any_of(
                 c("ID", "Description", "NES", "p.adjust", "setSize"))),
               file.path("interneurons",
                         paste0("interneuron_GSEA_", safe_name(cl), ".csv")))
  }
}
```

# Session

Resets the parallel plan, confirms the input object was not modified during the run, and records package versions for reproducibility.

```{r session_info}
future::plan(future::sequential)   # do not leak a parallel plan out of the notebook

# The input object must be byte-identical to what we started with.
cat("Input .rds unchanged:",
    identical(tools::md5sum(RDS_PATH)[[1]], "be1d0e281dacfdfb2b26d655d8860250"), "\n")

sessionInfo()
```
